description: Robots can already fold laundry, make espresso, clean kitchens, and assemble things. The harder problem is getting them to do those tasks reliably, for long periods of time, without a human babysitting them. At Startup School 2026, Physical Intelligence cofounder Chelsea Finn explains what it takes to build general-purpose robots that work in the real world. She shares how reinforcement learning pushed robot throughput up 2x, how their systems can run autonomously for hours, and why she believes…
classificationReason: Directly focuses on reliable general-purpose robots, reinforcement learning, autonomy, and cross-task generalization.
qualityReason: A focused technical talk with concrete reinforcement-learning methods, throughput and success-rate metrics, data ablations, generalization results, deployment constraints, and explicit discussion of model design tradeoffs.
